text: Reference tropopause 12 km; typically about 8 km at the poles to 16–18 km in the tropics. Most weather occurs here.
Ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation; temperature generally rises with height.
Temperature generally falls with height; many meteors become luminous here.
Shown only to 500 km. Its upper boundary varies with solar activity; the atmosphere continues beyond this view. Very high kinetic temperature does not mean dense hot air.
The beginning of this channel. Real headwaters can be springs, wet ground, snow or glacier melt.
A stream that joins another river.
The place where two channels join.
Water leaves this catchment at its outlet. A river mouth is where it enters a lake, sea or another receiving water body.
Solid rock. Oceanic crust is commonly 5–10 km thick; continental crust commonly 30–50 km. This reference section uses 35 km.
Mostly solid silicate rock. It deforms and convects over geological time; it is not a global magma ocean. Base: about 2,890 km depth.
Liquid iron-rich alloy, from about 2,890 to 5,150 km depth. Transmits P waves; it does not sustain ordinary shear (S) waves. Smooth metallic highlights are a material cue, not a map of flow.

Solid iron-rich alloy, radius about 1,221 km. High pressure allows it to remain solid at very high temperature. Fine grain and metallic highlights are illustrative material cues, not observed crystal sizes.
